newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends mixed in Europe, dealers focus on 120 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends mixed in Europe, dealers focus on 120 yen.

text.p: The dollar closed mixed in Europe as dollar/yen returned to the limelight, keeping upside pressure on the boil for a test of the closely eyed 120 yen level.

The U.S. unit rose to a fresh 47-month high of 119.69 yen in European trading but traders said talk of large option-related sell orders lined up at the 120 yen level and concern about Bank of Japan intervention kept the upside in check.

Talk that the Bank of Japan had been checking rates with several banks during European trading hours made the rounds, even though dealers doubted the central bank would would step in before a break of the 120 level.

"Dollar/yen moved more on rumours than on anything fundamental, and since it had some catch-up to do with dollar/mark it moved higher today while dollar/mark consolidated," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas.

Against the mark, the dollar spiked to a fresh 31-month high of 1.6455 marks but dealers said dollar/mark was in a consolidation phase for now. German M3 money supply data above market expectations put a dampener on dollar/mark.
M3 grew at an annualised 7.9 percent in December. M3 overshot its target of 4.0 to 7.0 percent in 1996, the Bundesbank said.
The M3 target range overshoot was widely expected, as was the Bundesbank's decision to keep key interest rates on hold and set another two repo tenders at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent.

Sterling recouped some of its sharp losses against the mark and the dollar after an overnight sell-off. Analysts said the pound had fallen prey to profit-taking by speculators after its sizzling rally.
"A lot of people simply decided to take some profits but the market is not selling the pound short," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in London.
At 1650 GMT dollar/mark was at 1.6400/05 marks and 119.58/63 yen compared with 1.6372/82 and 118.84/94 in late European trading on Wednesday.
Sterling traded at $1.6285/91 and 2.6695/05, well below late Thursday's levels of $1.6535/45 and 2.7090/00 but above its overnight lows of $1.6190 and 2.6610.
The sell-off was seen as position adjustment rather than a change in trend as solid UK fundamentals and sterling's still attractive yield will underpin the pound, analysts said.
